mathematical_review: Each individual length-m word has mass exp(-Nt)t^m/m!, without a spurious N^-m factor. Summing N^m words yields the Poisson(Nt) length mass and total mass one.
Time is nonnegative throughout. The empty word has mass one at t=0; an empty alphabet permits only the empty word for any time. The zero-length convention is preserved.
The latest event acts on the left: D_(w,i)=sqrt(I-k_i) D_w. This matches pinned chronology lines 49–54 and the source-inspected noncommuting two-factor regression.

The core algebraic hypotheses are k_i<=I, common annihilated Omega, arbitrary real g, and the operator lower bound. Positivity of k_i, g>0 and unit Omega are explained as source-application specializations.
Functional calculus makes sqrt(I-k_i) self-adjoint and fixes Omega; it therefore preserves Omega-perpendicular. The norm identity uses the real part of the Hermitian quadratic form.

The one-step and g>N conclusions need no k_i Omega=0. Each excited slice satisfies 0<=sum_i ||sqrt(I-k_i)v||^2<=(N-g)||v||^2, forcing zero when g>N. The spectator proof states this weaker argument directly.

Tensor products are physical operator on the left and spectator identity on the right. Finite coordinate slicing applies to arbitrary entangled inputs and introduces no spectator-dimension factor. Empty spectators and empty physical spaces are permitted where hypotheses are satisfiable.
The base excited-slice estimate allows arbitrary Omega; only the literal Q=I-|Omega><Omega| projection corollary requires ||Omega||=1. Its g<=N finite-word hypothesis is explicit.

For g<=N the nonnegative recurrence coefficient is N-g. The weighted sum is exp(-Nt)exp((N-g)t)=exp(-gt), for squared norms, with no extra factor two in the exponent. The g>N branch is settled by vanishing before using the comparison theorem.

Integrability is concluded from the nonnegative summable comparison, not assumed. The positive-time final consumer has a nonzero excited vector with initial energy one and t=g=1, bounding the actual expectation by exp(-1); source inspected only.

The paper is cited by title of its amplification section, not by an inferred section number from its filename. Estimate lines 237–253 and chronology lines 49–54 were read against the retained pinned manuscript.
The constructed normalized word measure is not identified with independent rate-one clocks. Coupled-clock locality and the full amplification theorem remain explicitly unproved.
